page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is an entry-tier virtual server within the High Performance family, configured with 1 shared x86_64 virtual CPU based on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. The compute allocation is paired with 2.0 GB of system memory, 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Discrete GPU hardware is not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-thread execution alongside constraints inherent to single-core provisioning. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1,421.58, which matches its multi-core result due to the single-vCPU limitation. PassMark benchmarking returned a CPU score of 1,616.42, an encryption score of 527.80, and a memory score of 742.08. Memory bandwidth measured 62.26 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached reads, shifting to 7.43 GB/sec uncached reads and 6.32 GB/sec writes under large 256 MB blocks. Synthetic compression workloads registered 23.24 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 8.10 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, while application tests recorded 1.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.85 GB/sec static web throughput.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GB memory ceiling, the server offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for baseline computing tasks, but lacks the parallel execution capability required for heavy multi-threaded loads. The included 50 GB NVMe storage provides low latency for disk I/O, offsetting compute bounds in file-access tasks. Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is well suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, dev/test environments, network monitoring nodes, and background worker queues.
description: The Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is an entry-level virtual server configured with 1 shared x86_64 Intel Xeon core operating at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates 16 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 1,421.58, an uncached memory read bandwidth of 7.43 GB/sec, and 1.62 million Redis SET operations per second. Without discrete GPU acceleration and restricted to a single shared vCPU, throughput is naturally constrained under parallel or sustained multi-threaded demands. However, the presence of responsive local NVMe storage delivers dependable disk I/O for lightweight systems. The instance functions effectively for cost-conscious, low-intensity workloads including static web hosting, basic API endpoints, simple database caching, and isolated software staging environments.
